ideas.title: Add Keyboard Shortcuts for Task Operations
ideas.description: Extend the existing keyboard shortcut pattern from the sidebar navigation to Kanban board task operations. Add shortcuts for common actions like opening task details (Enter), closing dialogs (Escape), marking tasks done (D), and moving to backlog (B).
ideas.rationale: The Sidebar component already has a well-established keyboard shortcuts pattern with the 'shortcut' property on navigation items (K for Kanban, A for Terminals, etc.). This pattern can be directly extended to task operations in the KanbanBoard component without architectural changes.
existing_patterns: App.tsx useEffect keyboard listener for project switching
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add useEffect keyboard listener in KanbanBoard for focused task shortcuts. 2. Track selected/focused task state. 3. Map key events to existing updateTaskStatus and selectTask actions from task-store. 4. Follow the same pattern as App.tsx global keyboard handling.

ideas.title: Add Task Export to JSON/CSV
ideas.description: Add export functionality for tasks in the Kanban board, allowing users to download their task list with all metadata in JSON or CSV format for backup or external tool integration.
ideas.rationale: All task data structures are already defined in shared/types/task.ts with comprehensive Task type. The task-store provides getTasksByStatus selector. The only missing piece is the download trigger, which is a trivial browser API call using Blob and URL.createObjectURL.
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add exportTasks utility function to lib/utils.ts that serializes tasks to JSON/CSV string. 2. Add export button in KanbanBoard header with dropdown for format selection. 3. Use Blob and URL.createObjectURL for download trigger.

ideas.title: Add Task Filters to Kanban Board
ideas.description: Add filtering capabilities to the Kanban board following the established ChangelogFilters pattern. Allow filtering tasks by creation date range, text search across title/description, and review reason.
ideas.rationale: ChangelogFilters.tsx demonstrates a mature filter UI pattern with RadioGroup selections, date inputs, and Select dropdowns. The KanbanBoard already has tasks as props and uses useMemo for processing - adding filter logic fits naturally into this flow.
existing_patterns: ChangelogFilters.tsx filter state management and UI structure
useMemo for derived task lists in KanbanBoard
Input component for search, Select for dropdowns
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add filter state (search term, date range, reviewReason filter) to KanbanBoard. 2. Create compact filter bar component inspired by ChangelogFilters sidebar pattern. 3. Apply filters in useMemo before column grouping using existing task properties. 4. Use existing Input, Select, Checkbox UI components.

ideas.title: Add Bulk Task Selection and Operations
ideas.description: Enable multi-select functionality for tasks in the Kanban board to perform bulk operations like moving multiple tasks to a different status, archiving, or deleting.
ideas.rationale: The Archive All button for Done column already demonstrates the bulk operation pattern. Checkbox component exists in ui/checkbox.tsx. The archiveTasks function in task-store shows multi-task operations are supported. This extends existing patterns to user-selectable scope.
builds_upon: Archive All button pattern in Done column
existing_patterns: Archive All button onClick handler in DroppableColumn
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add selectedTaskIds state to KanbanBoard. 2. Add checkbox to TaskCard (conditionally rendered based on selection mode toggle). 3. Add bulk action toolbar that appears when tasks selected. 4. Extend task-store with bulkUpdateTaskStatus action following archiveTasks pattern.

ideas.title: Add New Agent Tool Category for Task Analytics
ideas.description: Extend the backend tool registry to include task analytics tools that can provide insights on task completion rates, average time in each status, and bottleneck identification.
ideas.rationale: The tool registry pattern in agents/tools_pkg/registry.py shows a clean modular approach with create_*_tools factory functions (create_subtask_tools, create_progress_tools, create_qa_tools, create_memory_tools). Adding an analytics category follows the established factory pattern exactly.
existing_patterns: Tool function signature pattern with spec_dir and project_dir params
Tool return format from existing tool implementations
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Create new tools/analytics.py following tools/progress.py structure. 2. Add create_analytics_tools(spec_dir, project_dir) factory function. 3. Register in registry.py create_all_tools by adding all_tools.extend(create_analytics_tools(...)). 4. Implement get_task_metrics and get_completion_trends tools.

ideas.title: Add Keyboard Focus Rings to Task Cards
ideas.description: Task cards are interactive elements that can be clicked but lack visible focus indicators when navigating with keyboard. Add focus-visible ring styles matching the existing button focus pattern.
ideas.rationale: Keyboard users cannot currently see which task card is focused, making keyboard navigation difficult. This violates WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 2.4.7 (Focus Visible) which requires a visible focus indicator for keyboard-navigable elements.
ideas.current_state: TaskCard uses Card component with cursor-pointer but no focus-visible styles. When users Tab through the interface, the task cards appear selected but have no visual focus ring. The Card component in ui/card.tsx doesn't include focus styles.
ideas.proposed_change: Add 'focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-background' classes to the Card component in TaskCard.tsx. Ensure the Card element is focusable with tabIndex={0} and add role='button' aria-label={task.title} for semantic correctness.
ideas.user_benefit: Keyboard users can clearly see which task card is focused, enabling efficient keyboard navigation through the Kanban board without needing a mouse.

ideas.title: Add aria-labels to Icon-Only Buttons
ideas.description: Several icon-only buttons throughout the application lack proper aria-labels, making them inaccessible to screen reader users. The Add, Archive, and Help buttons are particularly affected.
ideas.rationale: Screen reader users cannot understand the purpose of icon-only buttons without aria-labels. Using only title attributes is insufficient as they are not reliably announced by screen readers. This violates WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
ideas.current_state: Icon-only buttons like Plus (add task), Archive, and Help use title={} for tooltips but lack aria-label attributes. Examples: KanbanBoard line 119-127 has Plus button without aria-label; line 129-137 has Archive button without aria-label. Sidebar Help button at line 348 also lacks aria-label.
ideas.proposed_change: Add aria-label to all icon-only buttons: 1) Add aria-label='Add new task to backlog' to Plus button in KanbanBoard DroppableColumn, 2) Add aria-label='Archive all completed tasks' to Archive button, 3) Add aria-label='Get help and support' to HelpCircle button in Sidebar. Pattern: <Button aria-label='Descriptive action label'>
ideas.user_benefit: Screen reader users can understand the purpose of each icon button and effectively navigate and interact with the application.

ideas.title: Add Live Region for Form Error Announcements
ideas.description: Form validation errors appear visually but are not announced to screen readers. Add aria-live regions to error messages in forms like TaskCreationWizard, AddProjectModal, and settings forms.
ideas.rationale: When form submission fails or validation errors occur, sighted users see the error but screen reader users are not notified. This creates a confusing experience where the form appears to do nothing. WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages) requires programmatic announcement of status changes.
ideas.current_state: TaskCreationWizard displays errors in a styled div (lines 1111-1116) but has no aria-live attribute. The error div contains visual styling with destructive colors but no semantic announcement mechanism for assistive technology.
ideas.proposed_change: Add role='alert' and aria-atomic='true' to error message containers. In TaskCreationWizard line 1111, update error div to: <div role='alert' aria-atomic='true' aria-live='assertive' className='flex items-start gap-2 rounded-lg bg-destructive/10 border border-destructive/30 p-3 text-sm text-destructive'>. Apply same pattern to all form error displays across the codebase.
ideas.user_benefit: Screen reader users are immediately notified when form errors occur, allowing them to understand what went wrong and take corrective action without visual cues.

ideas.title: Improve Touch Target Sizes for Mobile
ideas.description: Several interactive elements have touch targets smaller than the recommended 44x44px minimum, particularly image thumbnail remove buttons and column header icon buttons.
ideas.rationale: The image thumbnail remove buttons in TaskCreationWizard are 16x16px (h-4 w-4 class), significantly below the WCAG 2.5.5 recommended 44x44px touch target. This makes them difficult to tap accurately on touch devices and causes frustration for mobile users.
ideas.current_state: Image thumbnail remove buttons at TaskCreationWizard line 847 use 'h-4 w-4' (16x16px). Column header icon buttons in KanbanBoard use 'h-7 w-7' (28x28px). Both are below the 44x44px recommended minimum for reliable touch interaction.
ideas.proposed_change: 1) For image remove buttons: increase hit area using a larger wrapper while keeping icon visually small. Change 'h-4 w-4' button to 'h-8 w-8 p-2' wrapper containing 'h-3 w-3' icon. 2) For column header buttons: use 'h-10 w-10' (40px) which is closer to touch target minimum while keeping icon at 'h-4 w-4'. 3) Consider adding 'icon-lg' variant to button.tsx with 44x44px dimensions for critical touch targets.
ideas.user_benefit: Mobile and touch screen users can accurately tap small interactive elements without frustration or accidental misclicks, especially when removing image attachments or using Kanban column actions.

ideas.title: Add Collapsible Sidebar Navigation Sections
ideas.description: The sidebar has two fixed sections (Project and Tools) that cannot be collapsed. Allow users to collapse these sections to focus on relevant navigation items and reduce visual clutter.
ideas.rationale: Users working primarily with the Kanban board may not need to see GitHub Issues, PRs, or Worktrees sections constantly. Collapsible sections give users control over their workspace, reduce cognitive load, and are especially beneficial for users who prefer minimal interfaces. The Collapsible component already exists in the codebase.
ideas.current_state: Sidebar renders projectNavItems (7 items) and toolsNavItems (3 items) in fixed, non-collapsible sections. The collapsible.tsx component exists in ui/ folder and uses Radix UI but is not utilized in the Sidebar. Navigation is always fully expanded.
ideas.proposed_change:
Use the existing Collapsible component from ui/collapsible.tsx to wrap each navigation section. 1) Import Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger. 2) Add ChevronDown/ChevronRight icons to section headers. 3) Store collapse state in localStorage via useSettingsStore to persist preference. Pattern:
{projectNavItems.map(...)}
ideas.user_benefit: Users can customize their sidebar by collapsing sections they do not use frequently, creating a cleaner and more focused interface tailored to their current workflow.

ideas.title: Add Path Validation to File Explorer IPC Handler
ideas.description: The file explorer IPC handler in `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/file-handlers.ts` accepts arbitrary directory paths from the renderer via `listDirectory(dirPath)` and reads directory contents without validating the path is within allowed project boundaries. This could allow listing files outside intended directories.
ideas.rationale: Defense-in-depth requires validating paths in the main process even with context isolation enabled. While exploitation requires renderer compromise, the impact of unrestricted file listing could expose sensitive system files or other user data.
ideas.currentRisk: A compromised renderer could request listing of arbitrary directories, potentially exposing system files, credentials, or sensitive data outside project scope.

ideas.title: Add User-Facing Warning for Unencrypted Token Storage Fallback
ideas.description: In `apps/frontend/src/main/claude-profile/token-encryption.ts`, when Electron's safeStorage encryption is unavailable, OAuth tokens fallback to plaintext storage with only a console.warn. Users receive no notification that their credentials are stored insecurely.
ideas.rationale: OAuth tokens provide access to Claude AI services. Silent fallback to plaintext storage without user notification is a security anti-pattern. Users should make informed decisions about credential security, especially on systems without OS keychain support.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
ideas.currentRisk: On systems where safeStorage is unavailable (certain Linux configurations without a keyring daemon), OAuth tokens are stored in plaintext in settings.json, readable by any process with file access to the user's config directory.

ideas.title: Integrate npm Audit into CI Security Pipeline
ideas.description: The `.github/workflows/quality-security.yml` runs CodeQL and Bandit for code analysis but lacks npm dependency vulnerability scanning. The frontend has 35+ runtime dependencies (electron, xterm, @radix-ui components) that could contain known CVEs.
ideas.rationale: Supply chain attacks via npm packages are common. The project uses Electron v39, @xterm/xterm v6.0, react-markdown, and numerous UI libraries that should be continuously monitored. New CVEs are published regularly for popular packages.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-1104: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
ideas.currentRisk: Vulnerable npm dependencies could exist without automated detection. Electron updates frequently have security fixes that might be missed without automated monitoring.
ideas.remediation:
Add npm audit job to the security workflow:
```yaml
npm-security:
  name: NPM Dependency Audit
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '24'
    - run: cd apps/frontend && npm ci
    - run: cd apps/frontend && npm audit --audit-level=high
```
Consider using `npm audit --omit=dev` for production-only scanning and GitHub's built-in Dependabot alerts for continuous monitoring.

ideas.title: Use DOMPurify or rehype-sanitize for Release Notes Rendering
ideas.description: Two components use dangerouslySetInnerHTML with custom regex-based HTML escaping: `AppUpdateNotification.tsx` and `AdvancedSettings.tsx`. While the current implementation escapes <, >, & before processing markdown, regex-based sanitization is prone to bypass vulnerabilities.
ideas.rationale: Release notes content comes from external sources (GitHub releases API via electron-updater). Custom regex sanitizers often miss edge cases like malformed UTF-8, SVG-based XSS, or mutation-based attacks. Battle-tested libraries like DOMPurify have been tested against thousands of XSS vectors.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
ideas.currentRisk: If a crafted release note bypasses the regex sanitization (e.g., via mXSS), code could execute in the Electron renderer context. The current approach escapes &<> first which is good practice, but a whitelist approach is more robust.

ideas.title: Implement Python Dependency Hash Pinning for Supply Chain Security
ideas.description: The `apps/backend/requirements.txt` specifies dependencies with version ranges but lacks cryptographic hash pinning. This leaves the project vulnerable to supply chain attacks where a compromised package version could replace a legitimate one without detection.
ideas.rationale: Critical packages like claude-agent-sdk and graphiti-core handle AI credentials and execute in the backend context. Supply chain attacks on Python packages are increasing. Hash pinning ensures only verified, known-good package contents are installed.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-494: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
ideas.currentRisk: Dependencies are installed without cryptographic verification. A compromised PyPI package (via account takeover, typosquatting, or dependency confusion) could inject malicious code into builds.
ideas.remediation:
Use pip-compile from pip-tools to generate hashed requirements:
```bash
pip install pip-tools
pip-compile --generate-hashes requirements.in -o requirements.txt
pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt
```
Add pip-audit to CI for vulnerability scanning:
```yaml
- run: pip install pip-audit
- run: pip-audit -r apps/backend/requirements.txt
```
Consider adopting Poetry or PDM with lockfiles for better dependency resolution and security.

ideas.title: Add API documentation for agent modules
ideas.description: The apps/backend/agents/ module exports key classes (Planner, Coder, AgentSession) with minimal docstrings. Functions like run_agent_session(), create_client() and the agent lifecycle methods lack comprehensive documentation including parameters, return values, exceptions, and usage examples.
ideas.rationale: The agents/ module is the core of Turret's autonomous coding capability. Contributors need to understand agent lifecycle, session management, and how to extend agents. Currently developers must read source code to understand the API.
ideas.currentDocumentation: Module-level docstrings exist but function-level documentation is sparse. Only run_followup_planner() has comprehensive docstrings.
ideas.proposedContent: Add Google-style docstrings for all public functions including: parameters with types and descriptions, return types and meaning, exceptions raised, and usage examples. Create agents/README.md with architecture overview.

ideas.title: Create architecture diagrams for data flow
ideas.description: The project lacks visual architecture documentation showing how data flows between components: Frontend (Electron) → IPC → Backend (Python) → Claude Agent SDK → Memory/Graphiti. The CLAUDE.md has text-based structure but no diagrams.
ideas.rationale: New contributors struggle to understand the overall system architecture. Visual diagrams would accelerate onboarding and help developers understand where their changes fit in the broader system.
ideas.currentDocumentation: CLAUDE.md has text descriptions and folder structure. No visual diagrams exist for component interactions, data flow, or agent lifecycle.
ideas.proposedContent: Create Mermaid diagrams for: 1) High-level system architecture, 2) Agent execution pipeline (spec → plan → code → QA), 3) IPC communication between Electron and Python, 4) Memory/Graphiti integration flow. Add to CLAUDE.md or new docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

ideas.title: Add Graphiti memory integration guide
ideas.description: The Graphiti/LadybugDB memory system in apps/backend/integrations/graphiti/ lacks user-facing documentation. Configuration options (GRAPHITI_ENABLED, provider selection), usage patterns, and troubleshooting are undocumented.
ideas.rationale: Memory Layer is a key feature listed in README but users don't know how to enable, configure, or troubleshoot it. The env.example mentions it but lacks context on provider options (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Ollama, Google AI).
ideas.currentDocumentation: Only CLAUDE.md mentions Graphiti configuration briefly. No end-user guide for setup, provider configuration, or memory inspection.
ideas.proposedContent: Create guides/MEMORY-LAYER.md covering: 1) What the Memory Layer does, 2) Provider configuration (with examples for each), 3) Environment variables explained, 4) How agents use memory, 5) Viewing/clearing memory data, 6) Troubleshooting common issues.

ideas.title: Document frontend IPC handler API
ideas.description: The apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/ directory contains 20+ handler modules that define the Electron-to-Python communication API. These handlers have minimal JSDoc comments and no centralized API reference.
ideas.rationale: Frontend developers adding new features need to understand available IPC channels and their payloads. Currently they must search through handler files to discover available operations.
ideas.currentDocumentation: Individual README files exist in some subdirectories (github/, task/) but lack consistent API documentation. No unified reference for all IPC channels.
ideas.proposedContent: Add JSDoc to each handler function with @param, @returns, and @example. Create apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/API.md documenting all IPC channels, payloads, and response formats in a searchable table.

ideas.title: Add troubleshooting guide for common agent failures
ideas.description: The README has basic troubleshooting for installation issues, but lacks documentation for runtime agent failures: rate limits, stuck subtasks, QA loop failures, memory errors, and worktree conflicts.
ideas.rationale: Users encounter agent runtime issues but have no guidance on diagnosing or resolving them. Discord support shows recurring questions about rate limits, failed builds, and stuck QA loops that could be addressed by documentation.
ideas.currentDocumentation: README troubleshooting covers installation only. No runtime debugging guidance exists.
ideas.proposedContent: Create guides/TROUBLESHOOTING.md with sections: 1) Rate limit handling and auto-recovery, 2) Debugging stuck subtasks (PAUSE file, HUMAN_INPUT.md), 3) QA loop not approving (common criteria issues), 4) Worktree conflicts resolution, 5) Memory/Graphiti connection issues, 6) Reading debug logs (DEBUG=true DEBUG_LEVEL=2).

ideas.title: Implement React Component Memoization
ideas.description: Add React.memo and useMemo/useCallback hooks to prevent unnecessary re-renders in the frontend components, especially for components that receive complex objects as props or perform expensive computations.

ideas.title: Add Code Splitting and Lazy Loading
ideas.description: Implement React.lazy and Suspense for route-based code splitting in the Vite/React frontend to reduce initial bundle size and improve first contentful paint.

ideas.title: Optimize Zustand Store Subscriptions
ideas.description: Review Zustand store selectors to ensure components only subscribe to the specific state slices they need, preventing unnecessary re-renders when unrelated state changes.

ideas.title: Add API Response Caching
ideas.description: Implement caching strategies for backend API responses to reduce redundant computations and improve response times for frequently accessed endpoints.

ideas.title: Optimize Electron IPC Communication
ideas.description: Review and optimize Electron IPC calls between main and renderer processes, batch multiple small requests where possible, and consider using shared memory for large data transfers.

ideas.title: Split oversized TaskCreationWizard component into smaller focused components
ideas.description: The TaskCreationWizard.tsx component at 1166 lines is significantly over the recommended 400-500 line limit for React components. It handles multiple concerns: form state management, image attachments, file autocomplete, branch selection, model configuration, and draft persistence.
ideas.rationale: Large monolithic components are difficult to test, maintain, and reason about. Splitting into smaller, focused components improves reusability, testability, and makes code reviews easier. Each sub-component can be developed and tested independently.
ideas.currentState: Single 1166-line component handling: form state (title, description, metadata), image attachments with drag-drop, file autocomplete with @ mentions, Git branch selection, model/thinking configuration, and draft auto-save
ideas.proposedChange:
Extract into focused sub-components:
- TaskWizardForm.tsx (basic form fields)
- TaskImageAttachments.tsx (image upload/paste/drag-drop)
- TaskFileReferences.tsx (@ autocomplete and file explorer)
- TaskGitOptions.tsx (branch selection)
- TaskModelConfig.tsx (model and thinking level selection)
- useTaskDraft.ts (hook for draft persistence)
- useTaskForm.ts (hook for form state management)
ideas.bestPractice: Single Responsibility Principle - React components should do one thing well. Complex forms should be composed of smaller, reusable sub-components.
prerequisites: Ensure component has integration tests before refactoring

ideas.title: Consolidate large IPC handler files by extracting shared utilities
ideas.description: Several IPC handler files exceed 600-1000 lines: pr-handlers.ts (1133), worktree-handlers.ts (1003), autofix-handlers.ts (926), oauth-handlers.ts (832), execution-handlers.ts (816). These files contain similar patterns for subprocess execution, error handling, and IPC response formatting.
ideas.rationale: Large handler files with repeated patterns increase maintenance burden and risk of inconsistent error handling. Extracting common patterns into shared utilities reduces code duplication and ensures consistent behavior across all handlers.
ideas.currentState: Each handler file independently implements subprocess execution, progress callbacks, error formatting, and cleanup logic. The github/utils/ folder has some shared utilities but they're not consistently used.
ideas.proposedChange:
Extend the shared utilities pattern:
1. Create a createIPCHandler() factory that standardizes error handling and logging
2. Extract common subprocess execution patterns into subprocess-utils.ts
3. Create a progress-reporter.ts utility for consistent progress callbacks
4. Use a response-builder.ts for consistent IPC response formatting
ideas.bestPractice: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) - Extract common patterns into reusable utilities

ideas.title: Increase test coverage for renderer components
ideas.description: The frontend has only 18 test files covering the renderer, while there are 50+ component files. Critical components like TaskCreationWizard, KanbanBoard, App.tsx, and most store files lack dedicated test coverage. The existing tests are concentrated in main process and integration tests.
ideas.rationale: Low test coverage increases the risk of regressions when refactoring or adding features. Component tests enable confident refactoring and serve as documentation for expected behavior. The complex state management in stores like ideation-store.ts (757 lines) and task-store.ts (568 lines) would particularly benefit from unit tests.
ideas.currentState: 18 test files for frontend, mostly covering main process handlers and integration tests. Renderer components and Zustand stores have minimal coverage.
ideas.proposedChange:
Add test coverage for critical paths:
1. Store tests: Test state transitions, actions, and edge cases for ideation-store, task-store, changelog-store
2. Component tests: Add React Testing Library tests for TaskCreationWizard form validation, KanbanBoard drag-drop, App route switching
3. Hook tests: Test custom hooks like useVirtualizedTree (already has test) pattern for other hooks
ideas.bestPractice: Test Pyramid - Unit tests should form the base, covering critical business logic in stores and complex component behavior

ideas.title: Remove dead backup file and add git hooks to prevent future occurrences
ideas.description: A backup file changelog-handlers.ts.bk exists in the IPC handlers directory. Backup files should not be committed to version control and indicate a workflow issue. This type of file clutters the codebase and can cause confusion about which version is active.
ideas.rationale: Dead code and backup files in the repository increase cognitive load, can cause confusion during code reviews, and may accidentally be modified or imported. Git hooks can prevent these files from being committed.
ideas.currentState: Backup file (9125 bytes) exists alongside the main changelog-handlers.ts. The project uses Husky for git hooks but doesn't prevent .bk files.
ideas.proposedChange:
1. Delete the backup file: rm apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/changelog-handlers.ts.bk
2. Add to .gitignore: *.bk, *.backup, *.orig, *.old
3. Optionally add a pre-commit hook to warn about these patterns
ideas.codeExample:
# .gitignore additions:
*.bk
*.backup
*.orig
*.old
*~

# Optional: .husky/pre-commit addition:
#!/bin/sh
if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E '\.(bk|backup|orig|old)$'; then
  echo "Error: Attempting to commit backup files. Please remove them."
  exit 1
fi
ideas.bestPractice: Clean Repository - Version control should only contain production-ready code, not temporary or backup files

ideas.title: Split core/workspace.py into domain-specific modules to complete the refactoring
ideas.description: The workspace.py file at 1564 lines acknowledges it was 'refactored for better maintainability' with modules extracted to workspace/, but the main file still contains 'complex merge operations' that could be further extracted. The file has extensive import aliasing with underscores (_apply_path_mapping, _is_lock_file, etc.) indicating an incomplete refactoring.
ideas.rationale: The current state is a partial refactoring - models, utilities, and display functions were extracted but the core merge logic remains monolithic. Completing the refactoring would improve testability and make the merge system easier to maintain and extend.
ideas.currentState: 1564-line file with merge operations that 'reference each other' including: merge_existing_build, _try_smart_merge, _resolve_git_conflicts_with_ai, _run_parallel_merges, _merge_file_with_ai, _heuristic_merge. The file imports functions with underscore prefixes from its submodules.

Complete the refactoring by extracting the merge logic:
1. Create core/workspace/merge_operations.py for the merge_existing_build and related functions
2. Create core/workspace/ai_merge.py for AI-powered merge resolution (_merge_file_with_ai_async, _async_ai_call)
3. Create core/workspace/conflict_resolver.py for conflict detection and resolution
4. Update workspace/__init__.py to expose the clean public API
5. Remove the underscore-prefixed import aliasing
ideas.codeExample:
# Current imports (showing incomplete refactoring):

ideas.bestPractice: Single Responsibility Principle - Each module should have one clear purpose. Complete refactorings rather than leaving them half-done.
prerequisites: Ensure existing tests pass before refactoring
